content.comment_body: Hello, I'm looking for advice on how to reset a flag (such as M1) after setting it through the web interface. After starting a process using M1 from the web page, I want the program to automatically reset M1 so it’s ready for the next cycle a few seconds later. I'm unsure how to achieve this. Thanks.
It’s not possible to reset a flag within the [product_name] program if you set it remotely to 1. Please clarify which web interface you are referring to.
I’m referring to the web interface shown in my attachment. If automatic reset isn’t possible, how can I trigger a remote start for my program and ensure the start signal is set back to 0 afterward?
When setting a flag from the webserver, you can only reset it from the webserver. Please refer to the attached example.
A possible solution is to use a bit in the VM area.
Great, the solution works as I hoped. Thank you.

analysis.insight_summary: The user wanted to automatically reset a flag set via the web interface on a [product_name]. They realized the standard web interface doesn't support this functionality. Forum members explained the limitations and suggested utilizing VM bits as an alternate approach, which resolved the issue for the user.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that after starting a process remotely through the web interface, the system will automatically reset the start signal, enabling repeated operations without manual intervention. They also require a reliable method to trigger remote starts and confirm the signal resets for ongoing use.
